origin.description: Expose the names in the left-hand side to the right-hand expression.

arguments.name: lhs
arguments.text: A list, environment, or data frame whose names should be visible.

arguments.name: rhs
arguments.text: An expression that can use those names.

origin.details: Functions such as lm take a data argument and then see column names. This pipe gives that same convenience to an expression that has no data argument, by evaluating it with the left-hand side's names in scope.
origin.value: The result of the right-hand expression.

translation.description: Call a function with the mapping entries that match its parameter names.

arguments.name: mapping
arguments.text: A dict of names the function may use.

arguments.name: fn
arguments.text: A callable. Each parameter whose name is a key of mapping receives that value.

translation.details: Names the function does not declare are ignored. A parameter that is not in the mapping keeps its default, or the call fails if it is required. exposition({"z": [1, 2, 3]}, lambda z: sum(z)) is 6, matching data.frame(z = 1:3) %$% sum(z).
translation.example:
from magrittr.pipe import exposition
exposition({"z": [1, 2, 3]}, lambda z: sum(z))
